checked_claims.claim: Runner delegates invocation while supplying an app-loading object
checked_claims.reason: FlaskCliRunner is the Flask subclass of CliRunner, stores the same app, and delegates; no process or side-effect isolation guarantee is implemented here.

material_errors: Misidentifies FlaskCliRunner as the base runner and overstates isolation as preventing side effects between runs.
tasks.notes: Read the question/reference and relevant pinned-source code; static review only, no repository code executed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: FlaskCliRunner subclasses Click CliRunner, stores the supplied Flask app, defaults the command to app.cli, and supplies ScriptInfo(create_app=lambda: self.app) unless obj was supplied (src/flask/testing.py:265-298). ScriptInfo.load_app calls that callback and caches the app (src/flask/cli.py:333-372). The runner delegates actual invocation and testing-environment management to Click; this does not promise process isolation or prevent arbitrary app-state side effects.

checked_claims.claim: Hash lookup is delayed until wrapper invocation
checked_claims.reason: The wrapper accesses hashlib.sha1 only in its body; serializer construction receives the function, not its result.

material_errors: Incorrectly asserts serializer construction necessarily calls the digest wrapper.
tasks.notes: Read the question/reference and relevant pinned-source code; static review only, no repository code executed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: _lazy_sha1 accesses hashlib.sha1 inside the function body, so defining the function and assigning it as digest_method does not resolve SHA-1 during import. The docstring explicitly allows developers on FIPS builds to configure another digest before the wrapper is used (src/flask/sessions.py:290-307). get_signing_serializer passes the callable through signer_kwargs; the Flask code does not invoke it at serializer construction (src/flask/sessions.py:317-335).

checked_claims.claim: PassDict preserves keys and tags values
checked_claims.reason: The comprehension leaves keys unchanged; it does not stringify arbitrary key objects.

material_errors: Claims all Python dictionary keys are converted and preserve sufficient type information.
tasks.notes: Read the question/reference and relevant pinned-source code; static review only, no repository code executed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: PassDict.to_json leaves each key k unchanged and calls serializer.tag(v) for each value. Its comment states the reason: JSON objects may only have string keys (src/flask/json/tag.py:125-128). Tagged representations can preserve supported non-JSON value types, but this code supplies no key-type preservation or arbitrary-key conversion.

checked_claims.claim: Callback tracks dictionary mutation, not concurrent consistency
checked_claims.reason: Nested mutations require manually setting modified.

checked_claims.claim: Concurrent save ordering is unspecified
checked_claims.reason: Explicit documentation contradicts synchronization guarantee.

material_errors: False concurrency guarantee and claim all mutations are detected.
tasks.notes: Read the question/reference and relevant pinned-source code; static review only, no repository code executed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: It does not ensure consistency across concurrent requests. SecureCookieSession registers a callback that sets modified and accessed when its dictionary changes; nested mutable values require setting modified manually (src/flask/sessions.py:61-82). SessionInterface explicitly says concurrent requests may open and save in unspecified order (src/flask/sessions.py:141-146). The flag tracks a request session change; it is not a lock, merge mechanism, or cross-request consistency protocol.

checked_claims.claim: Context binding selects an AppContext-owned namespace
checked_claims.reason: An instance is allocated per AppContext, and push binds that same object; no cloning or lock is provided.

checked_claims.claim: g is a proxy to context .g
checked_claims.reason: Context lookup provides locality, not protection for a shared object.

material_errors: Overstates ContextVar as guaranteeing a new namespace per thread/task and thread-safe shared object access.
tasks.notes: Read the question/reference and relevant pinned-source code; static review only, no repository code executed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: _AppCtxGlobals is a plain namespace backed by __dict__ (src/flask/ctx.py:29-65). Each newly created AppContext creates a g object; push binds that AppContext with _cv_app.set(self), and pop restores the preceding binding (src/flask/ctx.py:245-265). The g LocalProxy resolves the current binding’s g attribute (src/flask/globals.py:24-33). Separately created and bound AppContexts therefore isolate namespaces. This does not make a shared AppContext or shared mutable values thread-safe or automatically clone them for every task.
